parts.article:
Robert Louis Stevenson
 
The writer of some of the best-known stories in the English language, including Treasure Island and The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
 
(A) It is more than 100 years since the death of the Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson on the South Pacific island of Samoa, and it seems that time has not been kind to Stevenson’s memory. Immediately after his death, his family and friends set to work to fashion the legend of Robert Louis Stevenson, or R. L. S., as he became known, one of the few writers familiar from his initials alone. Subsequent works of biography then turned him into a writer of almost religious importance. One example was literary critic Balfour, who in 1901 portrayed Stevenson’s family as ministering angels to the dying genius during his final illness. Similarly, the biographer Crouch absurdly overstated Stevenson’s significance by placing him in the same company as those most revered names in English literature: Shakespeare and Keats. The reaction to this nonsense was a number of highly critical assessments of Stevenson’s legacy in the 1920s.
 
(B) Normally, the critical pendulum can be relied on to swing back again, but there are several aspects of Stevenson’s work that have, until recently, acted against a more balanced appraisal. First is the allegation that Stevenson was a mere master of linguistic fireworks, who lacked moral depth. Some critics accused him of being a literary charlatan, of juggling words very prettily to strike effects which overawed an ignorant public, and served to distract from the inadequacy of his ideas.
 
(C) Then there has long been a prejudice against the adventure story as the proper medium for deep moral seriousness, a prejudice which is still extremely influential today. It seems that we can accept that an adventure film can successfully express profound moral truths, but we reject the same idea for a book. The absurdity of this becomes apparent when we think of writers like Joseph Conrad and Graham Greene, but it is no use pretending that this bias against adventure stories is not part of our high culture. A further problem is that Stevenson has often not found favour in the land of his birth because his conservatism so often collides with the strong radical tradition in Scotland. His many escapist stories and preference for living abroad have led to accusations that he camouflaged Scotland’s problems. Lastly, the high adventure of Stevenson’s own lifestyle has sometimes obscured his output, his life a greater story than any he could devise. This was precisely what his friends feared would happen towards the end of his short life: his art might be overwhelmed by the drama of life in Samoa.
 
(D) One consequence of this has been that Stevenson’s influence on other writers has too often been neglected. The writer and poet Oscar Wilde was deeply influenced by Stevenson, even though he declared that Stevenson would have produced better work if he had lived in London rather than Samoa. Stevenson tends to stick in the throat even of those writers who would like to spit him out, such as Shaw, who claimed to have learned from him that the romantic hero is always mocked by reality. Likewise, the writer Galsworthy, who began as a determined critic, later changed his mind and said that the superiority of Stevenson over the novelist Hardy was that Stevenson was all life and Hardy all death. The influence on the novelist Chesterton would also repay detailed study, for it was through him that Stevenson has managed to cross the ages, emerging as an influence on the modernist movement and our own contemporary Latin American school of “magical realism”.
 
(E) When making an assessment of his life and work one question must inevitably be asked: was Robert Louis Stevenson Scotland’s greatest writer of English prose? For most commentators this honour falls to Sir Walter Scott, author of Ivanhoe among many other classic novels, and it is true that in terms of craftsmanship, precision and the ability to minutely regulate language to create the desired effect, Scott takes the prize. However, this is not the same thing at all as inherent talent; by way of comparison one may take the example of the two great Russian composers Shostakovich and Prokofiev, of whom the former had learned more precise skills of execution but the latter’s intrinsic genius was greater, and so it seems to be with Scott and Stevenson. Admittedly, Scott’s detailed style does permit his stories to explore levels of tragedy that are beyond Stevenson’s reach, but in this regard they have the musty smell of the museum, somehow artificial and removed from modern day reality. On the other hand, Stevenson’s skill with plotting and narrative gives his books a timeless quality, so that they still live today, and Stevenson was also the shrewder judge of behaviour and psychology. For example, his compelling descriptions of a man with a split personality in The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde have proved so accessible and accurate that the expression “Jekyll and Hyde” has entered common English usage. Even if we do not see a revival of critical interest in this great Scottish writer, it is to be hoped that readers go back to Robert Louis Stevenson’s magnificent stories and reassess this neglected genius.

questions.question: In the opinion of the writer, the biographers Balfour and Crouch

analyses.content: 选项C说高估了“其他作家对他的影响”，但原文是把他“placed in the same company（并列）”而非谈论影响。
(Paragraph A) "...biographer Crouch absurdly overstated Stevenson’s significance by placing him in the same company as those most revered names..."
A段指出这两位传记作家把史蒂文森“捧得太高”：Balfour把他写成宗教般重要，Crouch则荒谬地夸大他的地位，把他与莎士比亚并列，对应选项 D（把他抬高到超过其真实地位）。

选项A说公众评价更公平，但原文说他用辞藻震慑了“愚昧的公众（ignorant public）”，并不是说公众评价公平。
(Paragraph B) "...served to distract from the inadequacy of his ideas."

analyses.content: C段作者认为尽管人们对书有偏见，但既然电影能表达深刻道德真理，书也可以，并举了Conrad等作家的例子来反驳偏见，暗示冒险故事能讲道理，选 B。
选项A说更适合电影，这是作者批判的“偏见（prejudice）”，而不是作者自己的观点；作者认为书和电影都应该被接受。
(Paragraph C) "We can accept that an adventure film can successfully express profound moral truths, but we reject the same idea for a book. The absurdity of this becomes apparent..."

analyses.content: (Paragraph C) "...because his conservatism so often collides with the strong radical tradition in Scotland."
C段中段提到他在出生地（苏格兰）不受欢迎，因为他的保守主义经常与苏格兰强烈的激进传统“发生冲突（collides）”，对应选项 A（观念与许多苏格兰人相反）。
选项D说他的故事让苏格兰人愤怒，原文只说他被指责“camouflaged（掩饰/伪装）”了问题，重点在于政治观念的冲突（collides）。

questions.question: According to the writer, Stevenson’s own lifestyle

analyses.content: C段末尾说他充满冒险的生活方式有时“掩盖了他的作品（obscured his output）”，生活本身比故事更像大片，对应选项 C（比书吸引了更多关注）。
“Obscured his output” 意为让作品显得黯然失色，即生活本身太抢眼了。
(Paragraph C) "The high adventure of Stevenson’s own lifestyle has sometimes obscured his output, his life a greater story than any he could devise."

questions.question: Although Oscar Wilde admired Stevenson’s work, he believed Stevenson could have written something better.

analyses.content: D段提到王尔德深受影响（admired），但也宣称如果史蒂文森住在伦敦而不是萨摩亚，他会写出“更好的作品（better work）”，选 YES。
“Produced better work” 直接对应题目中的 “written something better”。
(Paragraph D) "...even though he declared that Stevenson would have produced better work if he had lived in London rather than Samoa."

questions.question: Stevenson encouraged Oscar Wilde to start writing.

analyses.content: 文中只说了王尔德深受史蒂文森“影响（deeply influenced）”，从未提及史蒂文森是否“鼓励（encouraged）”他开始写作，选 NOT GIVEN。
“受到影响”不等于“受到鼓励去开始”，不要过度联想。
(Paragraph D) "The writer and poet Oscar Wilde was deeply influenced by Stevenson..."

questions.question: Galsworthy had greater respect for Hardy than Stevenson.

analyses.content: 看到“superiority of Stevenson over... Hardy”就要明白是史蒂文森胜出。
(Paragraph D) "...said that the superiority of Stevenson over the novelist Hardy was that Stevenson was all life and Hardy all death."
D段说Galsworthy改变了主意，认为史蒂文森对于Hardy的“优越性（superiority）”在于前者全是生命，后者全是死亡，即他更推崇史蒂文森，选 NO。

questions.question: More research is needed regarding Stevenson’s influence on Chesterton.

analyses.content: D段末尾说他对Chesterton的影响“值得详细研究（repay detailed study）”，意即应该进行更多研究，选 YES。
“Repay detailed study” 是学术英语中“值得深入研究/需要更多研究”的地道表达。
(Paragraph D) "The influence on the novelist Chesterton would also repay detailed study..."

groups.description:
Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 3?
In boxes 32–35 on your answer sheet write.

groups.contentHtml: Opinions differ as to whether Robert Louis Stevenson or Sir Walter Scott should be considered Scotland’s best writer. Scott had greater , but Stevenson had more , and the same distinction can be made between the two composers Shostakovich and Prokofiev. It is true that Scott’s books showed more when it came to tragedy, though in an old-fashioned way, while Stevenson’s books are still popular because of his . And Stevenson’s understanding of has resulted in the widespread use of an expression from one of his books.

analyses.content: E段对比时说，Scott在“craftsmanship（工艺）, precision（精确）”和“minute regulate language（细微调节语言）”方面更胜一筹，这些都属于技术控制，对应选项 F。
题目对应Scott的优点，原文的一连串词汇都是关于写作技巧的控制力。
(Paragraph E) "...in terms of craftsmanship, precision and the ability to minutely regulate language... Scott takes the prize."
(Paragraph E) "...but the latter’s intrinsic genius was greater, and so it seems to be with Scott and Stevenson."
题目转折说但史蒂文森有更多____，原文对比说后者（对应史蒂文森的位置）的“intrinsic genius（内在天赋）”更伟大，对应选项 A。
“Intrinsic genius” 完美对应 “natural ability”。
题目说Scott的书在悲剧方面显示了更多____，原文说Scott的风格允许通过故事探索史蒂文森无法企及的“levels of tragedy（悲剧的层次/深度）”，对应选项 H。
虽然原文没直接用depth，但“explore levels of tragedy”就是在挖掘深度。
(Paragraph E) "...permit his stories to explore levels of tragedy that are beyond Stevenson’s reach..."
题目说史蒂文森的书受欢迎是因为他的____，原文说由于他在“plotting and narrative（情节和叙事）”方面的技巧，对应选项 G。
“Plotting and narrative” 就是讲故事（storytelling）的核心要素。
(Paragraph E) "On the other hand, Stevenson’s skill with plotting and narrative gives his books a timeless quality..."
题目说他对____的理解导致了一个短语的流行，原文说他是“behaviour and psychology（行为和心理）”的精明判断者，对应选项 I。
“Behaviour and psychology” 统称为人性（human nature）。
(Paragraph E) "...Stevenson was also the shrewder judge of behaviour and psychology... ‘Jekyll and Hyde’ has entered common English usage."
